name: Suzanne "Suz" Seymour
bio: Suzanne Seymour is a Colchester, Vermont small-business owner, massage therapist and stand-up comedian who has also worked as a radio host and led the Vermont chapter of the American Massage Therapy Association. She is running as an independent for Vermont's at-large U.S. House seat and says she will not accept corporate PAC money.

platform.point: Target fraud and waste in federal spending to lower the tax burden on working Vermonters while protecting Social Security.
Shift toward prevention and wellness, expand mental health resources and give patients more healthcare choices.
Bring federal infrastructure funding to Vermont and support local businesses and job creation.
Push for election integrity, transparent government and accountability in the justice system.
Reduce the role of money and large corporate donors in politics.
Says she refuses corporate PAC money and pharmaceutical industry donations.
Wants federal investment in both physical and human infrastructure for the states.

liberty.evidence: General statement only: she describes herself as socially broad-minded, without naming positions on abortion, guns, drugs, LGBTQ rights or speech.

notes: Re-read the campaign home, About and Issues pages and searched VTDigger, Wikipedia and web search; the site covers taxes, waste, healthcare choice and investment only in general terms, so only a general liberty score was possible. No stated positions were found on immigration, foreign policy, energy, tech, education or religion.

name: Elizabeth Fitzgibbon
bio: Elizabeth Fitzgibbon is an independent candidate for Wisconsin's 6th Congressional District. Her campaign says she took a family law case through the courts to the U.S. Supreme Court and that the experience led her to run, promising a constitutional audit of federal government.

platform.point: Audit the Federal Reserve, fight inflation and support sound-money principles.
Crack down on waste, fraud and abuse and end federal spending she says drives up living costs.
Lower health care and prescription drug costs through more transparency and competition.
Protect Social Security and Medicare for seniors.
Reduce regulatory burdens on small businesses and farms and counter price-gouging through market competition.
Support expanding the housing supply so working families can stay in their communities.
Strengthen congressional ethics rules and require more disclosure of special-interest influence.
Judge each federal action first by whether the Constitution authorizes it; supports empowering citizen grand juries.

economy.evidence: Calls for cutting regulatory burdens on small businesses, ending excess federal spending, auditing the Federal Reserve and sound-money policy; these are general statements.

security.evidence: General statement only: lists exposing government surveillance among her transparency goals, without naming specific laws.

notes: Read the campaign home, About, Issues and Solutions pages; they focus on spending, inflation, costs and accountability, supporting only general economy and security scores. No stated positions were found on abortion, guns, immigration, foreign policy, energy, tech, education or religion.

name: Belinda Fox-Spencer
bio: Belinda Fox-Spencer is the Constitution Party nominee for West Virginia's 1st congressional district. She is described as a businesswoman and anti-abortion activist who ran as an independent in the 3rd district in 2020 and ran for the 1st district in 2022.
notes: Searched Wikipedia race pages, WV MetroNews and web search; no campaign website, questionnaire answers or issue statements were found. Her described anti-abortion activism was not scored without a stated policy position, so all topics remain unknown.
